Define the population

Start with the order cohort, return records, reporting period, and a consistent reason-code mapping. Decide whether the analysis counts returned orders, items, or units. The denominator must use the same level.

Ask Maia to flag records outside the cohort and reasons that do not map cleanly.

Build the review

Maia can compare return rates by product, period, or approved segment and show example reasons from the supplied records. It can separate operational errors from customer preference when the mapping supports that distinction.

Do not treat a return record as proof of refund completion. Keep order, return, and refund states separate.

Show counts with rates when cohort sizes differ. Ten returns can be a large signal for a small product and noise for a high-volume one. Maia can place the numerator and denominator beside each comparison.

Discuss patterns in Slack

Post the review where operations, merchandising, and support can challenge the mapping. A product owner may recognize that two free-text reasons describe the same sizing issue. An analyst can then revise the mapping and rerun the view.

A practical example

Footwear returns rise for the September cohort. Maia shows that size-related codes explain most of the movement, but twelve records use unmapped text. It also notes that the cohort denominator excludes orders still within the delivery window.

The operations analyst verifies the population before the team decides whether to investigate product copy, sizing, or fulfillment.

Keep the next step bounded

Use the review to choose an investigation. Maia can prepare questions and draft an internal update. It should not change product listings, inventory, or refund status without a separate authorized workflow.

Track changes to the reason-code mapping. If the team combines two codes, rerun the comparison or mark the break. Otherwise, classification can look like a customer trend.

Compare like periods and products. A new collection or holiday window can shift the mix enough to make a simple month-over-month rate misleading.

Document exclusions.

Common questions

Can Maia calculate a return rate?

Yes, from supplied records and a defined denominator. An analyst should verify cohort dates, units, and exclusions.

Can Maia explain why customers returned items?

It can summarize recorded reasons. Those codes may be incomplete or inconsistent, so preserve the sample limits.

Does a return mean a refund was paid?

No. Use the actual refund record when payment status matters.
